answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and two independent inherited memories (memory_86, memory_31) consistently show that simplifying/shortening onboarding produces durable activation and time-to-value gains for SMB accounts, making this the lowest-risk, highest-confidence lever for this week's single experiment slot. The competitor's aggressive entry pricing creates strong temptation toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records that a similar SMB discount produced a short-term signup pull-forward at the cost of -12pp retention and still owes a full readout — i.e., its long-term revenue impact is unresolved and likely net-negative for sustainable qualified revenue. I verified memory_73 to confirm this risk before ruling promotional_pricing out, and verified memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-simplification signal is a real, well-specified prior result (not just a paraphrase) before committing this week's capacity to it. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a plausible secondary candidate but onboarding completion decline is upstream of activation and has stronger, more corroborated evidence. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive don't address the acute SMB/onboarding pressure points this week.
